an4.73:1.1: “Monks, a person endowed with these four qualities can be known as ‘a person of no integrity.’
an4.73:1.3: “There is the case where a person of no integrity, when unasked, reveals another person’s bad points, to say nothing of when asked.
an4.73:1.4: Furthermore, when asked, when pressed with questions, he is one who speaks of another person’s bad points in full & in detail, without omission, without holding back.
an4.73:1.5: Of this person you may know, ‘This venerable one is a person of no integrity.’
an4.73:2.1: “And further, a person of no integrity, when asked, doesn’t reveal another person’s good points, to say nothing of when unasked.
an4.73:2.2: Furthermore, when asked, when pressed with questions, he is one who speaks of another person’s good points not in full, not in detail, with omissions, holding back.
an4.73:2.3: Of this person you may know, ‘This venerable one is a person of no integrity.’

an4.73:3.3: Of this person you may know, ‘This venerable one is a person of no integrity.’
an4.73:4.1: “And further, a person of no integrity, when unasked, reveals his own good points, to say nothing of when asked.

an4.73:4.3: Of this person you may know, ‘This venerable one is a person of no integrity.’
an4.73:4.4: “Monks, a person endowed with these four qualities can be known as ‘a person of no integrity.’
an4.73:5.1: “Now, a person endowed with these four qualities can be known as ‘a person of integrity.’

an4.73:5.5: Of this person you may know, ‘This venerable one is a person of integrity.’
